G9500.d: of three stories or floors , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9503.d: τροφο-φορέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Deu.1:31 (נָשָׂא), 2Ma.7:27 * ;] to nourish (Hesych.), bear like a nurse (R, mg., bare he them as a nursing-father): with accusative of person(s), Act.13:18, T, Tr., R, mg. (WH, R, txt., τροποφορέω, which see).† (AS)

G9506.d: 1. a vintage, harvest , (Plutarch) 2. the time thereof, the harvest or vintage , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9508.d: 1. to bore, pierce through , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., τὰ ὦτα τετρυπημένος having one's ears pierced for earrings , (Xenophon Historicus); ψῆφος τετρυπημένη the pebble of condemnation which had a hole in it , (Aeschines Orator) 2. τρ. τῷ ποδὶ τὴν βελόνην to force the point through the foot, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9510.d: 1. delicate, dainty , (Euripides), etc.:—; τὸ τρυφερόν effeminacy , ἐς τὸ τρυφερώτερον to more effeminate habits , (Thucydides):—;neuter as adverb, τρυφερόν voluptuously , (Aristophanes Comicus); τρ. λαλεῖν to speak softly , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9512.d: a hole formed by gnawing, a mouse's hole , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

G9513.d: 1. to make knobby :—;Pass., ῥόπαλα σιδήρῳ τετυλωμένα clubs knobbed with iron, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to make callous , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be callous , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9515.d: 1. a kettledrum , such as was used especially in the worship of Cybele, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a drum-stick : generally, a staff, cudgel , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. in Virgil tympana are wheels of solid wood. (ML)

G9517.d: 1. kingly power, sovereignty , (Pindar), attic; τ. ὑμῶν lordship over you, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. plural, αἱ τυραννίδες, = οἱ τύραννοι, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9519.d: 1. the good which man obtains τυγχάνει); by the favour of the gods, good fortune, luck, success , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; σὺν τύχῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); θείᾳ τύχῃ, Lat. divinitus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; hence Τύχη was deified, like Lat. Fortuna, Τύχη Σώτειρα (Pindar); T. Σωτήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. generally, fortune, chance , good or bad, in singular and plural, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 3. rarely of positive ill fortune , ἢν χρήσωνται τύχῃ, i. e. if they are killed, (Euripides); τύχῃ by ill-luck , (Antipho Orator) 4. especially, ἀγαθὴ τ. (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; in dative ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ "in God's name, " (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; by crasis, τύχἀγαθῇ (Aristophanes Comicus);—;this formula was also introduced into treaties, like Lat. quod felix faustumque sit, Λάχης εἶπε, τύχῃ ἀγαθῇ τῶν Ἀθηναίων ποιεῖσθαι τὴν ἐκεχειρίαν Decret. in (Thucydides):—;so ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῇ τύχῃ (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 5. Adverbial usages, τύχῃ by chance , Lat. forte, forte fortuna, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ἀπὸ τύχης (Aristotle Philosopher); ἐκ τύχης (Plato Philosophus); διὰ τύχην (Isocrates Orator), etc.; κατὰ τύχην (Thucydides), etc. 6. a chance, hap, accident , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τῆς τύχης, τὸ ἐμὲ τυχεῖν . . ! what a piece of ill-luck , that . . ! (Xenophon Historicus); mostly of mishaps, misfortunes , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G9520.d: the hyaena , an animal of the dog kind, with a bristly mane like a hog (whence the name), (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9523.d: 1. health, soundness of body, Lat. salus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;plural ὑγίειαι, healthy states or conditions , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of the mind, ὑ. φρενῶν soundness of mind, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9525.d: to wet, moisten , (Euripides): of a river, to water a country, (Euripides) (ML)

G9528.d: to draw, fetch or carry water , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Mid. to draw water for oneself, fetch water , πολῖται (Odyssey by Homer), attic (ML)

G9530.d: 1. carrying water , (Plutarch) 2. as Substantive, ὑδρ., a water-carrier , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9531.d: of or belonging to swine , ὑεία κοιλία pig's tripe, (Aristophanes Comicus):—; θηρίον ὕ., as a type of brutish ignorance, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9533.d: 1. to bark, bay, howl , of dogs, (Iliad by Homer); of hounds, to give tongue , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. metaphorically, κραδίη ὑλακτεῖ howls for rage , (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate to yell forth bold and shameless words , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἄμους᾽ ὑλακτῶν howling his uncouth songs, (Euripides) 3. transitive to bark at , τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9534.d: 1. woody, wooded , (Thucydides); τὰ ὑλώδη wooded ground , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. turbid, muddy , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9536.d: 1. to sing a hymn or song of praise : generally, to sing , ὑμν. θρῆνον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. = χρησμῳδέω, (Euripides)[ ῦ in (Aeschulus Tragicus)] (ML)

G9537.d: 1. as Substantive, ἐν ὑπαίθρῳ, entry Dio, in the open air , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. τὰ ὕπαιθρα, the field, the open country , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9538.d: 1. like Lat. summus for supremus, the highest, uppermost , of Zeus, ὕπατος κρειόντων, θεῶν ὕπ., (Homer); οἱ ὕπατοι the gods above , Lat. superi, opposite to οἱ χθόνιοι, Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατός τις some god above , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. simply of Place, ἐν πυρῇ ὑπάτῃ on the very top of the funeral pile, (Iliad by Homer) 3. of Time, last , Lat. supremus, (Sophocles Tragicus) 5. with genitive, like the preposition ὑπό, ὕπατος χώρας supreme over the land, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατοι λεχέων high above the nest, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 6. as Substantive, ὕπατος, the Roman consul , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G9546.d: to set up, prop up, support

G9548.d: 1. much like ὑπερηνορέων overweening, arrogant , (Iliad by Homer) 2. transitive to treat disdainfully , (Lucian) (ML)

G9551.d: 1. Dep. 2. to lie or be situate above , (Isocrates Orator) 3. to be postponed , (Lucian) (ML)

G9554.d: 1. exceeding long , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is very long, reaches very far , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. exceeding high , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry exceeding loud , (Pindar) (ML)

G9557.d: ὑπερ-οράω, see: ὑπερεῖδον. ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] to overlook: with accusative of thing(s), Act.17:30 (AS)

G9559.d: 1. to set higher, erect , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to set on the other side, carry over , (Plutarch) 3. in Mid. to hold over , so as to protect, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 4. metaphorically, παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set God over all, (Pindar) 5. to communicate a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperfect for -ετίθην); τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., especially in order to ask advice, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9565.d: 1. liable to give account for one's administration of an office, accountable, responsible , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts to public auditors λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. with genitive responsible for , ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is liable for their misdeeds, i. e. they must pay for them with their body, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with dative responsible to another, dependent on them, Lat. obnoxius, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9566.d: 1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew , (Thucydides), etc. 2. service , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9567.d: to put to sleep :—; Pass. to fall asleep, sleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9569.d: to look up from under the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously or angrily , Lat. limis oculis suspicere, (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast piteous glances , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be looked at with suspicion , (Euripides) (ML)

G9571.d: a garment under a coat of mail , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9573.d: 1. to burn by applying fire below , (Herdotus Historicus): to offer secret sacrifices , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. to light under , (Lucian) (ML)

G9576.d: 1. to lie under or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative, (Plato Philosophus) 2. in various metaphorically senses, 3. to be put under the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 4. to be laid down or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, (Plato Philosophus); impersonal, ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides) 7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus) 8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged or mortgaged , τινος for a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9581.d: 1. a remembrance, memorial , (Thucydides), etc. 2. a note, memorandum , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes , Lat. commentarii, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9584.d: to prick or sting underneath : generally, to sting , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9585.d: 1. to fall under or down, to sink in , (Plutarch) 2. to fall down before any one, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject to him, fall under his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to fall behind another, (Demosthenes Orator) 4. to get in under or among , (Thucydides) 5. of accidents, to happen, fall out , (Isocrates Orator) 6. of persons, to fall under a punishment, with dative, (Plutarch) 7. of places, to lie under or below , with dative, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9594.d: rendering service, serviceable, promoting, conducive to a thing, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9599.d: 1. indebted, in debt , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor , (Plutarch) 2. of property, involved , Lat. obaeratus, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. with genitive, ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)
